challenges.text: Spot Arundhati (Alcor) beside Vasishtha (Mizar) in the Saptarishi handle - an ancient eyesight test.
Count the stars of Krittika (the Pleiades) with bare eyes. Most people see 6 or 7; binoculars show dozens.
Compare the colours of Betelgeuse and Rigel - one orange, one blue-white - opposite corners of Orion.
Find the Andromeda Galaxy from a dark spot - the farthest thing your naked eye can see.
Watch Jupiter's four Galilean moons line up like tiny stars, then check tomorrow to see them move.
Hold binoculars steady on Saturn until the rings make it look like a tiny oval.
Trace Orion's Belt - Alnitak, Alnilam, Mintaka - then follow the line down-left to Sirius.
Look below Orion's Belt for the 'middle star' of the sword that is not a star - the Orion Nebula.
Note the Moon's colour when it is near the horizon, then again high in the sky.
Count the stars of Saptarishi, then use the two outer bowl stars to point five fists up to Dhruva (Polaris).
Walk around the Winter Hexagon: six of the sky's brightest stars ringing Orion.
Sweep the Milky Way's brightest stretch with binoculars and find any nebula or cluster - then log which one.
